units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
CHEVELEY
units.name: MRS

units.text: Rising .
I don’t mind waiting in the carriage at all, provided there is somebody to look at one.
units.name: MRS

units.text: Well, I hear the curate is always prowling about the house.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: I am afraid I am not fond of girl friends.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: LADY CHILTERN [ Rising .] Oh, I hope Mrs. Cheveley will stay here a little.
I should like to have a few minutes’ conversation with her.
How very kind of you, Lady Chiltern! Believe me, nothing would give me greater pleasure.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Ah! no doubt you both have many pleasant reminiscences of your schooldays to talk over together. Good-bye, dear Gertrude! Shall I see you at Lady Bonar’s to-night? She has discovered a wonderful new genius. He does . . . nothing at all, I believe. That is a great comfort, is it not?
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Robert and I are dining at home by ourselves to-night, and I don’t think I shall go anywhere afterwards. Robert, of course, will have to be in the House. But there is nothing interesting on.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Dining at home by yourselves? Is that quite prudent? Ah, I forgot, your husband is an exception. Mine is the general rule, and nothing ages a woman so rapidly as having married the general rule.
units.name: LADY MARKBY

units.text: Exit LADY MARKBY.

Wonderful woman, Lady Markby, isn’t she? Talks more and says less than anybody I ever met. She is made to be a public speaker. Much more so than her husband, though he is a typical Englishman, always dull and usually violent.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Makes no answer , but remains standing .
There is a pause .
Then the eyes of the two women meet .
LADY CHILTERN looks stern and pale .
MRS. CHEVELEY seem rather amused .
Mrs. Cheveley, I think it is right to tell you quite frankly that, had I known who you really were, I should not have invited you to my house last night.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: CHEVELEY
units.name: MRS

units.text: With an impertinent smile .
Really?
units.name: MRS

units.text: I could not have done so.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: I see that after all these years you have not changed a bit, Gertrude.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: I never change.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: CHEVELEY
units.name: MRS

units.text: Elevating her eyebrows .
Then life has taught you nothing?
units.name: MRS

units.text: It has taught me that a person who has once been guilty of a dishonest and dishonourable action may be guilty of it a second time, and should be shunned.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Would you apply that rule to every one?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Yes, to every one, without exception.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Then I am sorry for you, Gertrude, very sorry for you.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: You see now, I was sure, that for many reasons any further acquaintance between us during your stay in London is quite impossible?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: CHEVELEY
units.name: MRS

units.text: Leaning back in her chair .

Do you know, Gertrude, I don’t mind your talking morality a bit. Morality is simply the attitude we adopt towards people whom we personally dislike. You dislike me. I am quite aware of that. And I have always detested you. And yet I have come here to do you a service.
units.name: MRS

units.text: Contemptuously .
Like the service you wished to render my husband last night, I suppose. Thank heaven, I saved him from that.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Starting to her feet .
It was you who made him write that insolent letter to me? It was you who made him break his promise?
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Yes.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Then you must make him keep it. I give you till to-morrow morning—no more. If by that time your husband does not solemnly bind himself to help me in this great scheme in which I am interested—
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: This fraudulent speculation—
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: Call it what you choose. I hold your husband in the hollow of my hand, and if you are wise you will make him do what I tell him.
units.name: MRS. CHEVELEY

units.text: Rising and going towards her .
You are impertinent. What has my husband to do with you? With a woman like you?
units.name: LADY CHILTERN

units.text: CHEVELEY
units.name: MRS

units.text: With a bitter laugh .

In this world like meets with like. It is because your husband is himself fraudulent and dishonest that we pair so well together. Between you and him there are chasms. He and I are closer than friends. We are enemies linked together. The same sin binds us.
units.name: MRS

units.text: How dare you class my husband with yourself? How dare you threaten him or me? Leave my house. You are unfit to enter it.
units.name: LADY CHILTERN
